source_excerpts.text:
Statement
---------
Consider k equal-frequency canonical bosonic modes with Hamiltonian
H = hbar*omega*sum_i a_i^dagger a_i. Initially their state is tau_n tensor k,
where n = (exp(hbar*omega/(k_B*T))-1)^(-1), and T>0 is the sole preparation
reservoir temperature. Work storage and Hamiltonian control are explicit
resources. All Hamiltonians return to H after preparation.

For an arbitrary final state rho, define its normal second-moment matrix by
N_ij = Tr(rho a_j^dagger a_i). Impose N_ii=n for all i. No Gaussian assumption
is imposed on rho. Let P be a rank-r orthogonal projector, 1<=r<k, with
P_ii=r/k. For a chosen 0<=nu<n, require P N P <= nu P. These are occupation
constraints on a selected set of r canonical collective modes; they do not
assert a quantum communication capacity or a complete converter specification.

Define g(x)=(x+1)ln(x+1)-x ln x, with g(0)=0, and
b=(k*n-r*nu)/(k-r). Then every admissible state satisfies

S(rho) <= r*g(nu)+(k-r)*g(b).

Consequently its free-energy increase over the initial product thermal state is
at least

Delta F >= k_B*T * [k*g(n)-r*g(nu)-(k-r)*g(b)].                 (1)

The entropy and free-energy bounds are attained by a phase-insensitive Gaussian
state with N_star=nu*P+b*(I-P). Equation (1) is therefore the exact minimum
free-energy increase in this state-preparation problem. It is a lower bound on
average preparation work, and a reversible-work infimum with ideal global
quasistatic controls. It is not a finite-time or bounded-control work equality.
At nu=0, perfect vacuum preparation requires a limiting protocol.

Proof
-----
Choose an orthonormal basis of modes adapted to ran(P) and ker(P). The total
occupation in the first r modes is t=Tr(PN)<=r*nu; the others have total
occupation k*n-t. A single bosonic mode with mean occupation x has entropy at
most g(x). One proof compares its state with tau_x by nonnegativity of relative
entropy; log(tau_x) is affine in the number operator. Subadditivity and the
concavity of g therefore give, without any Gaussian assumption,

S(rho) <= r*g(t/r)+(k-r)*g((k*n-t)/(k-r)) = F(t).

For 0<t<=r*nu<r*n,
F'(t)=g'(t/r)-g'((k*n-t)/(k-r))>0,
because g'(x)=ln(1+1/x) decreases and the first occupation is below n while
the second is above n. Continuity covers t=0. Thus F(t)<=F(r*nu).

In the adapted basis take r independent thermal modes of occupation nu and
k-r independent thermal mode

   Delta F_min/(k_B*T)
   = r*ln(n)+r-(k-r)*ln(k/(k-r))-r*g(nu)+o(1).
   More ports can reduce a constant term; they do not remove the r*ln(n)
   leading cost. If nu scales proportionally with n, this expansion is not
   the relevant regime. The low-occupation resource is a requirement, not a
   proof of a large engineering energy penalty.

3. Independent warm loss of transmissivity eta on every delivered port gives
   N_delivered=eta*N_star+(1-eta)*n*I. Selected occupation is therefore
   eta*nu+(1-eta)*n. A target nu_target requires
   1-eta <= nu_target/n even with perfect source cooling. This is a favorable
   equal-loss, equal-temperature model; colder injected loss is a different
   resource ledger.

4. For one selected unit vector u, a misaligned converter vector v gives
   v^dagger*N_star*v = nu+(b-nu)*(1-|u^dagger*v|^2).
   Thus delivering occupation <=nu_target requires
   1-|u^dagger*v|^2 <= (nu_target-nu)/(b-nu).
   For two equal weights with phase error delta and nu=0, this is
   2*n*sin(delta/2)^2. No stability/calibration service is supplied for free.

5. The same laboratory carrier frequency is load-bearing. Different-frequency
   mixing needs a pumped converter, and its work, noise and heating must be
   added. Changing damping to a common-bath dark-mode model also changes the
   input-output plant. The result does not prohibit consistent decoherence-free
   interactions, measured feedback, squeezed ancillas or other encodings.

6. A matched source-resource comparison is available in the same ideal global
   control model. Directly cool r thermal modes from n to nu, leaving the other
   k-r modes at n. Its reversible-work infimum is

   W_cold/(k_B*T)=r*[g(n)-g(nu)+(nu-n)*ln(1+1/n)].

   Write W_bal for (1). Then exactly

   (W_bal-W_cold)/(k_B*T)=(k-r)*D(tau_b || tau_n)>=0,
   D(tau_b || tau_n)=(b-n)*ln(1+1/n)+g(n)-g(b).

   The identity follows from (k-r)*(b-n)=r*(n-nu); nonnegativity is the Gibbs
   relative-entropy inequality. Thus keeping all physical ports locally hot

source_excerpts.text:
The candidate was a microwave-to-optical converter whose two thermal inputs are correlated, so their thermal contributions cancel at the converted output without cooling either local marginal. A successful device could make a warm mechanical intermediary compatible with transfer of an unknown quantum state. The consequential barrier is laser-pump heating plus thermal injection in transducers that connect superconducting processors to optical fiber.

The current nearest model is [Hou et al., arXiv:2608.06683v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2608.06683v1), especially Eqs. (3), (6), (7), (17), (26), and (34). It supplies a phase-insensitive cross moment between mechanical and microwave input noises, then tunes scattering phases for cancellation. [Hou et al., Phys. Rev. Research 7, L032042 (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.13790) already establishes the corresponding direct-transduction proposal. No novelty is claimed for this effect.

## Exact task contract

Input: an unknown single-rail qubit in the span of vacuum and one microwave photon. The validation input is one half of `( |0_R 0_A> + |1_R 1_A> ) / sqrt(2)`, so successful classical coherent-signal subtraction does not suffice. All trials count; no postselection is used.

For a transparent favorable model, let the useful channel be

`a_out = sqrt(eta) a_in + sqrt(1-eta) d`,

where `d` is a canonical bath mode, independent of the input qubit, with a thermal state of occupation `n_d`. At `eta = 0.8`, the route should achieve entanglement fidelity at least 0.85. This is a stated target, not a measured device parameter. Bandwidth, duty cycle, source preparation, qubit encoding, decoder, and absorbed pump energy must be reported separately. A claim of positive capacity additionally requires an appropriate energy-constrained coding analysis; low added noise alone is insufficient.

The supplied/calibrated plant includes the full scattering matrix versus frequency, independent loss rates and temperatures, accessible bath-port couplings, correlation spectrum, and delay/phase fluctuations. These must be acquired experimentally, including both quadratures and any anomalous moments. An exact covariance or exact bath routing is not a free input to an end-to-end technology claim.
